title: T1/T2 Mapping in Pericarditis: A Retrospective Study for the Determination of Diagnostic Cut-off Values
summary: Cardiac MRI has become established as a valuable tool in the diagnosis of pericarditis. It provides evidence of inflammatory changes in the pericardium. In recent years, T1 and T2 mapping have also gained additional importance, as they allow more precise assessment of tissue changes. In previous studies, inconsistent results were found regarding elevated and reduced T1 values. The aim of this study is to retrospectively investigate whether threshold values for T1 and T2 times can be defined in patients with confirmed pericarditis that may be useful for future diagnostics.

interventions.name: Retrospective monocentric study with evaluation of existing cardiac MRI datasets including T1-/T2-mapping of the pericardium in 30 patients with confirmed actue pericraditis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
MRI with STIR hyperintensity and late enhancement in the pericardium without evidence of myocarditis (according to modified Lake Louise criteria).
Availability of T1-/T2-sequences.
Diagnosis of acute pericarditis in the clinical context. 
Age  ≥ 18 years.
Exclusion criteria:
Incomplete imaging data.
Missing mapping sequences.
Poor image quality.
Patients with coexistence of other myocardial pathologies.
